_comment: Real VA multi-hazard comparison. Deploy a copy of this file to <soge_clusters parent>/hazards.json on Hopper (sibling of soge_clusters, matching config_hopper.json/lodes_data layout), or point RESIFLOW_HAZARDS_MANIFEST at it directly. Rasters must already be aligned via scripts/align_hazard_rasters.py under inputs/va_multihazard_aligned/<hazard_subtype>/event_1.tif. Landslide's event_1.tif is NOT a raw aligned raster -- it's the output of scripts/compute_landslide_pgd.py (HAZUS PGD from susceptibility + PGA), see that script and src/resiflow/hazards/landslide_pgd.py.

events._note: VA DCR 1% annual chance (100yr) depth grid, feet->meters, aligned to EPSG:9311 @ 50m.

Real 2011 Mineral, VA M5.8 USGS ShakeMap PGA (scripts/prepare_shakemap_pga.py) -- default earthquake source since 2026-08-03 via resolve_real_source()'s hazard_type->RealEarthquakeShakeMapSource mapping (src/resiflow/hazards/real_va.py); this note previously described the older NSHM-contour-rasterized default and was stale. The pre-2026-08-03 NSHM source is still reachable via RESIFLOW_EARTHQUAKE_SUBTYPE=earthquake_nshm for comparison/rollback. 2026-08-19: confirmed via ScienceBase (curl with a normal browser user-agent -- the earlier '404' was Cloudflare bot-blocking an automated client, not a missing dataset) that the official 2023 NSHM gridded/GIS ground-motion product does exist and is downloadable; a raw 0.2-degree point-grid CONUS product (item 03 of the 2023 NSHM ScienceBase release) is also available and would let a future CONUS-wide (non-VA-specific) earthquake run use interpolated real NSHM values instead of contour rasterization, if/when that's needed. closure_threshold=25 is the existing placeholder (g x100?) -- see fragility/earthquake_categorical.py's own _MAJOR_PGA/_MINOR_PGA thresholds (0.10-0.45g), which are what actually classify damage; this scenario-level closure_threshold is a secondary, coarser cutoff and should be reconciled against those before trusting results.

NOAA SNODAS snow depth, 2016-01-23 (Winter Storm Jonas peak day), meters->mm, aligned to EPSG:9311 @ 50m. closure_threshold=100mm is the testbed placeholder -- sanity-check against this event's actual aligned value range before trusting results.

HAZUS Newmark PGD (mm), computed by scripts/compute_landslide_pgd.py from USGS n10 CONUS susceptibility (clipped/aligned, equal-width-binned from its native 0-81 count into HAZUS None/I-X via --susceptibility-max-count 81) + the real 2011 Mineral, VA ShakeMap PGA (inputs/va_multihazard_aligned/earthquake_shakemap_mineral/event_1.tif -- the same source earthquake_401 uses by default), at scenario magnitude M=5.8. RECOMPUTED 2026-08-19: the original PGD (computed 2026-07-26, one week before the ShakeMap PGA source existed on 2026-08-03) had used the older, coarser NSHM contour-rasterized PGA instead and was never regenerated -- every landslide_501 result up to this point understated peak displacement by roughly 9x (107mm vs the corrected 945mm) and could never reach fragility/landslide_categorical.py's 'severe' bucket (150-300mm threshold) anywhere in VA. Corrected range: ~0.1-945mm nonzero (0.1% of cells -- ShakeMap's sharp epicenter-centered decay vs. NSHM's broad smoothed hazard curve, a real shape difference, not just a magnitude one). closure_threshold=100mm is still the testbed placeholder; reconcile against the categorical thresholds before trusting results, same caveat as earthquake's closure_threshold.
